freeze_boundary: Draft only. Materializes exactly the API-003 acceptance rule: stable ordering, no duplicate or missing item between pages, and an opaque cursor. The >=2 sort keys requirement is a DECLARED INFERENCE from asset-library-database-ux-spec-th.md section 5.2, which specifies the keyset cursor (created_at, id) and prohibits deep offset. TAMPER-SAFETY IS NOT ENFORCED: the cursor encoding, signing algorithm and key management are unspecified in the baseline and are NOT invented here, so a forgeable cursor is accepted - see accepted_gaps. No page-size bound exists in the baseline. Per-entity sort fields and filter grammar belong to the owning module contracts and are not inferred.

accepted_gaps.examples/accepted-gap-decodable-offset-c: This cursor base64-decodes to "offset=40&limit=20". The contract ACCEPTS it. API-003 calls the cursor "opaque/tamper-safe", but no integrity mechanism is specified in the baseline and this contract does not invent one, so opacity-by-inspection is all that holds. The fixture exists to keep that gap visible until an owner specifies a MAC or signature.
accepted_gaps.examples/accepted-gap-unbounded-page-siz: page_size 500. The contract ACCEPTS it. No maximum page size appears anywhere in the Sprint 0A baseline. An earlier draft of this package invented a bound of 100; that was removed as unsourced. The bound is a real enumeration-risk control and is referred to the contract owner.

untestable_by_fixture: API-003 requires "no duplicate or missing item between pages". Every items array in these fixtures is empty, so fixture inspection cannot demonstrate that property at all; it needs a real dataset and a paging harness. The manifest previously read as if the rule were materialized. It is declared here as NOT demonstrated, and must be proven by an integration test before freeze.
untestable_by_schema: Distinct sort FIELDS. JSON Schema uniqueItems compares whole items, so it cannot require one property to be distinct across items. Enforced by test-kits/contracts/shared-kernel-envelope-contracts.test.mjs instead. Recorded because an earlier version of that test asserted 1 < 2 and never touched the contract at all, so a fixture with created_at twice passed green.
